page.name: Appointment reminders
page.h1: Send reminders people turn up to
page.metaTitle: Appointment reminder messages that reduce no-shows
page.metaDescription: Confirmation plus a timed reminder on the number the appointment was booked with, with opt-out rules that leave the reminders alone.
page.lede: A reminder earns its place by arriving early enough to change a plan and saying only what the person needs to act on: when, where, and how to change it. Send a confirmation at booking and a timed reminder before, on the number they booked with.

bullets: Confirmation at booking — the appointment exists and is recorded
Reminder a fixed interval before — the appointment is soon
A one-tap way to reschedule or cancel, in the message itself
p: The reminder is transactional: it confirms something the recipient already arranged. That matters, because opt-out suppression applies to promotional traffic rather than to a reminder someone needs in order to turn up.

sections.h: Spread the reminder hour across your numbers
p: Reminder traffic clusters — most of it goes out at the same hour the day before. Because provider limits apply per sender number, a clinic-sized batch can queue behind itself, so the useful planning question is how many sender numbers the reminder hour needs.

sections.h: Keep the detail out of the message
p: A reminder is not a place for clinical, financial or case detail. The platform does not store message bodies — the log is metadata only — but the message itself still travels through your provider and lands on a handset that may be shared. Send a reference the recipient resolves in your own system rather than the detail itself.

faq.q: Can someone opt out of reminders entirely?
faq.a: Suppression applies to promotional traffic. If you want to let people opt out of reminders, that is your own preference model rather than the platform’s suppression rule.
You can connect the accounts you hold on each channel and choose per send. Routing and suppression as described here are SMS-channel capabilities.

faq.q: How do we know a reminder arrived?
faq.a: A delivery receipt is recorded against the send wherever the provider reports it back. It confirms the network accepted the message, not that the recipient read it.
